keyA.notes: p156 ends with a complete paragraph (prayer ٨١), so p157 has a plain marker; no footnote continues. Divine Names in red marked ==…== (عَفُوُّ، رَءُوفُ، مَالِكَ الْمُلْكِ، ذَا الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ). In red الْجَلَالِ (p159) the round sukun on ل touches the fatha on ج; read as sukun+fatha. الْأَكْوانَ on p157 has no fatha on و (fatha present on p158 الْأَكْوَانِ). وَلِوَالِدِيْنَا on p159 has a sukun on ي as printed. A stray small dot below the text on p159 (about 44% page height) was treated as a print speck and omitted. Quran (آل عمران ٢٦، الأنبياء ١٠٧، النمل ٦) encoded per Tanzil Uthmani, checked against print (waqf ۖ after تشاء and الخير printed). p160 ends mid-sentence (continues on p161). Headings on p160: ## صلوات اليوم السادس, ### الصلاة البرزخية, ### صلاة التجلي. All small harakat were verified at 1100-1800 dpi zooms since 480 dpi renders dropped some fathas.

keyB.notes: p157 starts a new item (٨٢) so no '+' marker; no footnote continues from p156. آلِه is printed with a single kasra (on lam only) on pp.157-159, but آلِهِ with two kasras on p160. Quran on p158 uses dotless ى in تُؤْتِى and شَىْءٍ and the ۖ sign after تَشَآءُ and ٱلْخَيْرُ. A stray dot in the empty area of p159 was ignored. The whole divine name مَالِكَ الْمُلْكِ (p158) and ذَا الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ (p159) is red. p160 has no red text.
